reviews.review: It's a great game that provides a ton of replayability and fun, especially with friends. The gameplay is satisfying and intuitive, with great gun play, countless built options for all classes, and incredible class synergy. To be totally successful, you need all classes present in this game, which is rarely the case in heavily meta focused titles such as Destiny 2. Reward system is okay, overclocks for your weapons are the main rewards and incentives in this game. Would like to see some additional non-gameplay oriented incentives such as titles for completing difficult missions x amount of times or just simply a title system in which you complete various achievements for a title for your character, just like in Destiny.

The Best [b]"Barrel Kicking Simulator 2019"[/b]!
But Dwarves look [b]ugly[/b] :c
So...[u][b]NO![/b][/u]

Treat this game as something similar to Left 4 Dead. You have hordes attacking you, and need to complete objectives to get out before they overwhelm you. If you go down, you can be picked back up, but will have next to no health once you do get back up. You have unlimited downs, but trust me when I say all 4 dwarves being downed is common in this game (it is the lose condition after all). Certain dwarves struggle against specific enemy types, and building to counter that weakness will make you weak to something else. Unless you're a *really* good player overall, SOMETHING will be a nuisance to you in this game. These weaknesses can be negated by sticking close to your teammates, and working together as a team to get through the horrors of Hoxxes.

The game excels as a team-based game, and I consider it to be my current favorite coop title. It's a good time running from a horde of a hundred Glyphids as your whole downed team is getting pounded into the floor by 3 Oppressors.


Do be warned though, that you will have seen all of the content the game has to offer at only a few hundred hours. I have as many as I do from wanting to get Gunner to Legendary. The game is incredibly grindy with not really enough gameplay content to warrant replaying as much as I have. Expect a few hundred hours, and unless you're really committed, you will start getting bored like I did.

Updates are slow, non-cosmetic content even slower. Mods definitely help this, though.


I'd add more here, but at that point, I should be making a Deep Rock Galactic Ultimate Guide. It's a good title, like with Left 4 Dead 2. Pick it up, even at full price. It's 100% worth the purchase.

Great community, but it does tend to show its ass whenever there's too many new players at once (Christmas, free play weekends, etc.)

The game itself is a tight experience with loose mechanical balance, so you can make practically any loadout work. It's teamwork, and not the specific guns, that the devs expect you to bring.
